primary_sources: Herbert Hoover, address accepting the Republican presidential nomination, August 11, 1928

stimulus.text: “We in America today are nearer to the final triumph over poverty than ever before in the history of any land. The poorhouse is vanishing from among us. We have not yet reached the goal, but, given a chance to go forward with the policies of the last 8 years, we shall soon with the help of God be in sight of the day when poverty will be banished from this Nation.” — Herbert Hoover, speech accepting the Republican presidential nomination, August 11, 1928. Abridged.
stimulus.source_note: Herbert Hoover, address accepting the Republican presidential nomination, Stanford, California, August 11, 1928. Verbatim excerpt, abridged; public domain.

stem: Hoover's claim that poverty would soon be banished rested on

options.text: a promise to expand the federal government greatly
options.misconception: Hoover praised limited government and private enterprise. Expanding the federal government was the opposite of his program.

options.text: a plan to end all private business at once
options.misconception: Hoover celebrated business and individual effort. Ending private business was never his plan.

options.text: continuing the Republican policies of the last eight years
a call for America to join the League of Nations
options.misconception: Hoover never calls for joining the League in this speech. The League was a dead issue by 1928.

rationales.A: Hoover praised limited government and private enterprise. Expanding the federal government was the opposite of his program.
rationales.B: Hoover celebrated business and individual effort. Ending private business was never his plan.
rationales.C: Hoover's own words tie the promise to 'the policies of the last 8 years,' the Republican record under Harding and Coolidge. He asks voters to keep those policies going.
rationales.D: Hoover never calls for joining the League in this speech. The League was a dead issue by 1928.
rationales.general:
1. Find the condition in Hoover's sentence: 'given a chance to go forward with the policies of the last 8 years.'
2. Ask whose policies those were. Background: the Republicans held the White House under Harding and Coolidge.
3. Ask what he promises if they continue: poverty banished from the nation.
4. Name the base of the claim: eight years of Republican rule.
Remember: a promise that names a condition rests on that condition, so quote the condition.
